title: The Value of a Human Life

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If someone is caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite and treating or selling them as a slave, the kidnapper must die. You must purge the evil from among you. - Deut 24:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God addresses the terrible crime of kidnapping, stealing a person to enslave or sell them. Under Israel's law, this was a capital offence. Why so severe? Because a human being is not property to be seized and sold. To kidnap and traffic a person was to treat someone made in God's image as a mere object for profit, a grievous assault on human dignity.

This law reveals how highly God values every human life. People are not commodities. The trafficking and enslaving of human beings is a profound evil in God's eyes, because it violates the sacred worth He has given to each person. God's justice rose up strongly to defend the dignity and freedom of the vulnerable individual.

While we do not carry out such civil penalties today, God's heart on this matter has not changed. Human trafficking and the exploitation of people remain grave evils that God hates. Every person bears His image and possesses inherent, God-given worth (Gen 1:27). The gospel affirms this dignity in the strongest terms, for Christ gave His own life to redeem people, showing how precious each soul is to God. We are called to value people as God does, never using or exploiting them, and to stand against the ways human beings are still bought, sold, and abused in our world. How can you honour the God-given dignity of every person, and stand with the exploited?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you value every person as bearing God's image?
2. How does Christ's costly love show human worth?
3. How can you stand against the exploitation of people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that every person is precious to You. Help me honour the dignity of all and stand against every exploitation of human life. Amen.
